correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for all integer sample sizes by Gamma–Dirichlet decomposition, exact shared exponential min covariance via survival integrals, rank-one normalization, circulant diagonalization, strict analytic inequalities, and a one-dependent central limit theorem. At n=2 the degenerate pair is handled separately. Independent deterministic quadrature plus reproducible simulations check the formulas but do not certify the infinite statements.

Jiao–Gao–Han (2017), Theorems 1–2, bound torus entropy-estimator risk, not exact finite covariance.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Those more general asymptotic statements already cover the order 1/n variance and near-2.14 numerical limit; neither determines every finite-n covariance entry, its sign, or the finite-sample trigamma correction without a new computation. We claim no new general CLT or numeric asymptotic order.

value.rationale: An exactly computable finite-null second-moment covariance, as opposed to asymptotic 2.14 and risk bounds, supplies practical finite standard errors and reveals a strict local-positive/nonlocal-negative dependence mechanism with a nontrivial, strictly positive Fourier spectrum for a natural entropy estimator. It supports null calibration and interpretation, without claiming exact quantiles, unproved nonuniform properties, or a new general estimator.
